patterns: Registry pattern: a new language needs a grammar entry, a handler module with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, an extract_inheritance function, and arms in get_language_info and get_ts_language (languages/mod.rs).

java.rs ELEMENT_QUERY (literal): "(method_declaration
  name: (identifier) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (identifier) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (identifier) @interface_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (identifier) @enum_name) @class
"
java.rs extract_inheritance: reads child_by_field_name('superclass') and child_by_field_name('interfaces'), emits 'extends X' and 'implements X' strings.
swift.rs extract_inheritance: iterates node.child(i) for inheritance_specifier children (no field names), first one becomes 'extends', later ones 'conforms'.

parser_elements.rs capture names: 'function' plus 'func_name' or 'method_name' for functions; 'class' plus 'class_name' or 'type_name' for types; the handler is called only when a 'class' capture matches.
parser.rs compiles DEFUSE_QUERY only when defuse_query is Some; fortran uses None, so DEFUSE_QUERY is optional at the type level.
tree-sitter-php grammar: 'name' is the node kind used for declarations and member names (no 'identifier' kind exists in php/src/node-types.json); variables are variable_name whose child is name.

approaches.name: A: Full Java/Swift mirror with LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to workspace and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; create languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression, each capturing name as @call), REFERENCE_QUERY ((named_type (name) @type_ref)), IMPORT_QUERY ((namespace_use_declaration) @import_path), DEFUSE_QUERY (see defuse_query_draft), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children; register in mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info arm with extract_inheritance only, get_ts_language arm using LANGUAGE_PHP) and lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP row, supported_languages entry); add unit tests, an ImportTestCase row, and the MCP integration test.
pros: Matches the five-query contract the issue asks for and the Java template
DEFUSE_QUERY gives local-variable and parameter write sites for the defuse path

cons: Largest diff: about 8 files plus Cargo.lock

Import text stored by the parser fallback arm includes 'use' and the semicolon unless a dedicated arm is added

recommendation: Approach A. It matches the issue's five-query scope and the Java/Swift templates, and every node kind and field used was confirmed in the grammar (common/define-grammar.js and php/src/node-types.json) and by parsing sample files with tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 through the Python binding: element query (6 patterns), call query, import query, reference query, defuse query, and inheritance walk all compile, and the mixed HTML sample and the class/interface/trait/enum/static/global/foreach samples produce zero ERROR nodes with LANGUAGE_PHP. DEFUSE_QUERY is optional at the type level (LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option and fortran passes None), so it is required by the issue's query scope and by the defuse test pattern used in java.rs and python.rs, not by the compiler. Verify the crate's crates.io publish date against the 7-day age rule before adding the Cargo.lock entry.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source: php/src/node-types.json and common/define-grammar.js (lines 334-337 base_clause, 339-346 enum_declaration, 365-372 class_declaration, 381-384 class_interface_clause, 326-332 interface_declaration). Walk, from a class_declaration node: (1) iterate node.child(i) over all children (neither clause has a field name, so child_by_field_name cannot be used); (2) for a child of kind 'base_clause' (grammar: keyword('extends') then commaSep1($._name)), iterate its named children; each child of kind 'name', 'qualified_name' or 'relative_name' yields 'extends <text>'; (3) for a child of kind 'class_interface_clause' (grammar: keyword('implements') then commaSep1($._name)), iterate its named children and yield 'implements <text>' for the same three kinds. The class_declaration children list in node-types.json is: abstract_modifier, base_clause, class_interface_clause, final_modifier, readonly_modifier, static_modifier, var_modifier, visibility_modifier; the body is the field 'body' of kind declaration_list. Interface declarations use base_clause (multiple 'extends'); enum declarations use class_interface_clause only. Verified with the Python binding: 'class Dog extends Animal implements ICanRun, ICanSwim {}' yields ['extends Animal', 'implements ICanRun', 'implements ICanSwim'] and 'class Plain {}' yields []. Note the class name is field 'name' of kind 'name', not 'identifier'.
